newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss banker not guilty in money laundering case.
newsitem.headline: Swiss banker not guilty in money laundering case.

text.p: A Swiss court on Friday found a senior banker not guilty of laundering money for Colombian drug smugglers in a case which had been seen as the first big test of tough laws passed in 1990.
But the court ordered the banker to return some 1.6 million Swiss francs ($1.1 million) he earned for managing the Colombians' money.
The banker, Josef Oberholzer, went on trial last month on charges of managing Swiss accounts for the drug smugglers for nearly 15 years.
The portfolio he oversaw had grown to $150 million by the time he was arrested and the money was seized in 1994.
The 63-year old former Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) vice-director was the highest-ranking banker in Switzerland to be charged with such a crime.

The $150 million was the largest haul of alleged laundered money ever in Switzerland and prosecutors saw the case as the first big test of laws to combat money laundering that Switzerland passed in 1990.
"It could not be proven that he acted intentionally," Zurich district attorney Dieter Jann said. He said only intentional money laundering activities were punishable by law.

He explained the court order to return the 1.6 million francs on the grounds that proceeds from illegal activities could be recovered independent of a decision on whether or not a defendant's activities were punishable by law.

The banker's lawyer did not deny his client managed the drug money. But he argued that handling the funds constituted negligence, since Oberholzer did not know where the cash was coming from and did not inquire, and negligence in such cases was not punishable by law.
Zurich prosecutors had been seeking a prison sentence of two-and-a-half years and a fine of 200,000 Swiss francs. ($ = 1.477 Swiss Francs)
